editorial:
Looking for something cozy and magical to watch with the family? You get two classic stories here that feel like a digital storybook. First, you follow a poor miller's daughter who gets into a scary deal with a greedy little troll to save her dad. Then, you switch gears to a funny tailor who accidentally becomes a local hero after killing some flies. Both stories have a whimsical, old-school vibe that makes you feel like you are sitting around a campfire listening to legends. The characters are colorful, and the worlds are bright and imaginative, making it an easy watch for a lazy Sunday afternoon.

What really works here is how the movie keeps things moving quickly so you never get bored. The voice acting is great, and the way the tailor tricks the giants is genuinely funny. While the animation might look a bit dated compared to today's big studio movies, it still has a lot of charm. If you want the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the colors pop. Or, if you love owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great call for movie nights.
endingExplained: In the first story, the queen finally discovers the troll's strange name just in time, which breaks his spell and lets her keep her baby. In the second story, the tailor uses his quick wit to outsmart the giants and the wild boar. He proves that being smart is better than being strong. He wins the heart of the princess and lives happily ever after in the castle.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic fairy tales and family-friendly animation.
